title: The Talking Tree
summary: Two partners dispute a bag of gold, and one claims a sacred tree spoke from heaven to endorse his claim. Birbal lights a fire to reveal the 'tree's voice.'
full_text:
Two trading partners, Ram and Shyam, buried a bag containing two thousand gold mohurs beneath a hollow peepal tree outside Agra, agreeing that neither would touch the money without the other present.

A month later, when they went to retrieve the treasure, the hole was empty. Shyam cried: 'Ram, you dug it up in secret and stole the gold!'

Ram denied it vehemently, swearing on his children.

Shyam said: 'Let us appeal to the sacred peepal tree itself! That tree is inhabited by an ancient celestial spirit who sees all things. If the tree names you as the thief before Emperor Akbar, will you accept the judgment?'

Ram, confident in his innocence, agreed.

The next morning, Emperor Akbar, Birbal, courtiers, and village elders gathered around the colossal peepal tree.

Shyam stepped forward, bowed reverently, and cried: 'O Sacred Tree! Reveal the truth! Who stole the gold buried beneath your roots?'

To the utter astonishment and horror of Emperor Akbar and the crowd, a deep, hollow voice echoed from within the trunk of the tree:

'RAM IS THE THIEF! RAM DUG UP THE GOLD AT MIDNIGHT!'

The crowd gasped. Akbar was shaken: 'A tree that speaks! Ram, confess your crime!'

Ram fell to his knees, weeping: 'Sire, I am innocent! I do not know how a tree can speak!'

Birbal stood observing the ancient tree. He noticed a faint opening between two roots covered with freshly gathered moss, and saw that the soil near the back of the trunk was disturbed.

Birbal smiled calmly: 'Your Majesty, if this tree is indeed a sacred celestial spirit, it deserves a grand Vedic offering of incense and fragrant smoke to honor its divine wisdom.'

Birbal ordered four bundles of dry straw and pungent chili peppers placed around the hollow base of the tree, and struck a flint to ignite them!

Dense, choking clouds of smoke billowed into the hollow opening of the trunk.

Within thirty seconds, violent coughing broke out from inside the tree trunk: *Cough! Wheeze! Choke! Have mercy! I am burning!*

A scrawny man tumbled out of the hollow opening, gagging on smoke and rolling on the grass!

It was Shyam's elderly father! Shyam had hidden his father inside the hollow tree before dawn to play the part of the 'divine voice'!

The crowd erupted in outrage. Shyam and his father fell at Akbar's feet, confessing their treacherous conspiracy.

Akbar ordered the stolen gold recovered, confiscated Shyam's property, and praised Birbal's sharp eyes for smoking out the fraud.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Talking Tree"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
